problem: The equation ${m}^{2}+8=-8m$ can be written in the form $(m+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $p+q,$ and solve the equation.

feedback.problem: The equation ${t}^{2}+10t+13=0$ can be written in the form $(t+p)^{2}=q.$   Find $p+q.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side and complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}+10t+13 & =0 \\ {t}^{2}+10t & =-13 \\ {t}^{2}+2\cdot 5\cdot t & =-13 \\ {t}^{2}+2\cdot 5\cdot t+{5}^{2}-{5}^{2} & =-13 \\ (t+5)^{2}-25 & =-13\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we isolate the perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}(t+5)^{2}-25 & =-13 \\ (t+5)^{2} & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $p=5,$ $q=12,$ and $p+q=17.$
